newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market preopening report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market preopening report.

text.p: Spanish debt market is positioned to make losses on Monday opening after the left's win in French elections, dealers said.
They added the Spanish market will likely take a small step back awaiting firmer indications of policy from future French prime minister Lionel Jospin.
"We'll be on stand by, to see what the new government really intends to do," said Alfredo Urrutia, economist with Societe Generale in Madrid.
The peseta, which fell to a record low at 84.91 per mark, was trading at around 0645 GMT at 84.81/84 per mark.
That was lower than Friday's close at 84.64/67.
"If the peseta should break 85 per mark, it's likely the Bank of Spain will step in, checking prices, more in order to stop volatility than aiming at a level," said Urrutia.
Madrid-based analysts were focusing on what the left win means for the European economic and monetary union.

"We'll either have a soft euro or no euro at all," said Hernik Lumholdt, adding that now, after the Bonn-Bundesbank standoff, the most likely scenario seems to be a softer French version of the forthcoming euro.
A softer approach to Euro would increase chances of Spain qualifying in the first wave of monetary union.
